RATIÉ CH. 4 — THE SELF, THE COGNITIONS, THEIR RELATION

  • er-chapter analysis for the thesis. Source lines 12230–14549. Where the Pratyabhijñā
  • ands among the ātman-controversy; the asymmetry of Self and cognitions; identity as
  • namism.*

1. THE CHAPTER'S THESIS

  • e Self is immanent in yet transcendent to its cognitions (asymmetric relation); the
  • gnition of the "I" is a cognition of recognition (pratyabhijñāpratyaya); identity is
  • t unity but dynamism (svātantrya). Recognition is an experience, not a construction.

2. EXTENDED QUOTES (French verbatim + English translation)

Q1 — The "I" is a cognition of recognition (lines 12272–12281)

"cette cognition du Je est une 'cognition qui est une reconnaissance'
(pratyabhijñāpratyaya)… c'est le fait que je me reconnais comme le sujet qui a perçu dans
le passé… ('c'est moi qui ai perçu et qui me souviens à présent de X')."
**"this cognition of the I is a 'cognition that is a recognition' (pratyabhijñāpratyaya)…
it is the fact that I recognize myself as the subject who perceived in the past…
('it is I who perceived and who now remembers X')."**
  • → THE THESIS NODE.** The most basic self-cognition IS a recognition — the felt
  • lf-grasping across time.

Q2 — Recognition is intuitive, not conceptual (lines 12315–12351)

"il y a dans le souvenir une reconnaissance de soi qui n'est pas le fruit d'une
construction conceptuelle… mais d'une saisie intuitive de soi… 'moi qui ai perçu ceci
[autrefois], je perçois cela [à présent]'."
**"there is in memory a self-recognition that is not the fruit of conceptual
construction… but of an intuitive self-grasping… 'I who perceived this [before], I
perceive this [now]'."**
  • →** Recognition is felt (intuitive), not abstract. Pairs with the felt-is-primary.

Q3 — The asymmetric relation; immanence + transcendence (lines 13139–13167)

"Le Soi est donc à la fois synthèse et agent de la synthèse… immanent aux cognitions, il
est leur unité… transcendant les cognitions, il est liberté (svātantrya) de les
différencier et de les unifier. Il y a… une asymétrie fondamentale… (si la cognition n'est
que le Soi, le Soi, lui, ne se réduit pas à la cognition)."
**"The Self is therefore at once synthesis and agent of the synthesis… immanent to the
cognitions, it is their unity… transcending the cognitions, it is the freedom
(svātantrya) to differentiate and unify them. There is… a fundamental asymmetry… (if the
cognition is nothing but the Self, the Self does not reduce to the cognition)."**
  • →** The bearer is immanent + transcendent. The felt cannot be reduced to its objects.

Q4 — The pure synthesis at the heart of the impure (lines 13944–13972)

"si nous sommes capables de nous souvenir, c'est précisément parce que la conscience
absolue ne perd jamais conscience d'être conscience absolue… provoquer une reconnaissance
(pratyabhijñā) par laquelle le sujet empirique… retrouve l'identité avec le Soi qu'il n'a
jamais vraiment perdue."
**"if we are capable of remembering, it is precisely because absolute consciousness never
loses consciousness of being absolute consciousness… to provoke a recognition
(pratyabhijñā) by which the empirical subject… recovers the identity with the Self it has
never really lost."**
  • → THE THESIS.** Recognition = the recovery of an identity never really lost, evoked
  • rough the lived memory-experience. The felt always already present.

Q5 — Identity = dynamism (svātantrya) (lines 14009–14013, 14425–14449)

"l'identité ne saurait être conçue comme une pure et simple unité… c'est le dynamisme de
la conscience… l'identité, c'est la capacité à se différencier tout en restant un – ou la
liberté (svātantrya) de se manifester comme Autre sans cesser d'être Soi."
**"identity cannot be conceived as a pure and simple unity… it is the dynamism of
consciousness… identity is the capacity to differentiate oneself while remaining one — or
the freedom (svātantrya) to manifest oneself as Other without ceasing to be Self."**

Q6 — Recognition is an experience, not an abstract construction (lines 14358–14368)

"une reconnaissance (pratyabhijñā) qui… n'est pas une pure et simple construction
abstraite, mais une expérience… la conscience ne perd jamais totalement conscience d'être
conscience."
**"a recognition (pratyabhijñā) which… is not a pure and simple abstract construction but
an experience… consciousness never totally loses consciousness of being consciousness."**
  • → THE THESIS NODE.* Recognition is a *felt experience, not a construction. This is
  • actly the paper's claim — and the felt-is-primary.

3. IPK LINKS

  • ĪPK 1.3.7 — the unifier/asymmetry doctrine (Q3).
  • ĪPK 1.6.3 — the Self as relation between manifestation and its modes (Q3 context).
  • The pratyabhijñāpratyaya (cognition of the I) — the aham-pratīti of ĪPK I.2, elevated.

4. THESIS LITERATURE-REVIEW VALUE

  • The "I" is a recognition (Q1, Q2) — the paper's core: the most basic self-cognition
  • a felt re-cognition.
  • Recognition is experience, not construction (Q6) — the direct refutation of the
  • ddhist view and the paper's felt-is-primary.
  • Identity as dynamism (Q5) — the felt is dynamic activity, not static; pairs with
  • st-recognition re-rendering.
  • The never-lost identity (Q4) — recognition recovers what is always already felt.

5. IPVV TRANSLATION HOOKS

  • pratyabhijñāpratyaya (the recognition-cognition) — the "I" as recognition.
  • anusandhāna / anusandhātṛ (synthesis / synthesizer) — the asymmetry.
  • āśraya (substrate) — the bearer.
  • svātantrya (freedom) — identity as dynamism.
  • aham / idam (I / this) — the aham-idam split (felt vs object).
  • h4 is where recognition is shown to be a felt experience (Q6), the "I" a recognition
  • 1), and identity a dynamism (Q5). The "never really lost" identity (Q4) is the felt
  • ways already present. This is the paper's recognition-as-felt foundation.*
